stimulus.text:
| City | Region | Approximate population at its height |
| Tenochtitlan (Mexica) | Central Mexico | About 200,000 |
| Cahokia (Mississippian) | Mississippi River valley, near present-day St. Louis | About 20,000 |
stimulus.source_note: Approximate figures; Cahokia about 20,000 at its peak in the 1200s and Tenochtitlan about 200,000, consistent with standard estimates (see grounding).

stem: The table gives city sizes. Other evidence shows Cahokia's mounds, plazas, and palisade, and Tenochtitlan's temples and tribute system. Taken together, what do these pieces of evidence show?

options.text: Both cities were small farming villages with almost no public organization.
Large populations and monumental building went together in both of these cities.
City size alone proves both cities shared the same single government.
The evidence shows both cities depended on European trade alone.

instruction: Pick one option from the stimulus and stem only. Do not open the question file.
